full_judgment:
15. Election rights are not common law rights. They are the creation of a statute and should be exercised only in the manner in which the law which create them provided. In the course of the arguments the learned Advocate for the opposite party did not    dispute the correctness of the said proposition of law but he has contended that the bar of jurisdiction of   the Civil Court is conditional on the existence or functioning of the tribunal created by the special law. In support of this contention he has relied on the decision in the case of Sat Narain Gurwala-Vs.- Hanuman Parshad and another, A.I.R. 1946 Lahore 85 where it has been observed thus: 

 22. Section 26 of the Ordinance provides that no election under this Ordinance shall be called in question except by an election petition under sub- section (2) and that any candidate may make an election petition in the prescribed manner to the Election Tribunal appointed under section 27 challenging election at which he was a candidate. Section 29 lays down that the decision of the Election Tribunal on the petition shall be final subject of the decision of the District Judge. An appeal provided for in Sub-Section (4), Rule 45 enumerates the relief which the petitioner may claim in the election petition. Under Rule 48 the Tribunal shall have all the powers of the Civil Court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure. Rule 48 indicates that the Election Tribunal shall be competent to give reliefs mentioned in Rule 45 or make such orders as it may think fit but the Election Tribunal shall not declare the election of any returned candidate or the election as a whole void unless it is satisfied that the result of the election has been materially affected by reason of the failure of any person to comply with or the contravention of these rules. The Ordinance and the Rules made thereunder, clearly provide for a special forum in the Election Tribunal to determine the election dispute which is to be brought before the Election by an election petition after the publication of the result in official Gazette under Rule 41. The contravention of Rules during election process can however, be made a ground to call the election in question by filing election petition.
